name: Make small talk with strangers
blurb: Small talk is not trivia, it is the protocol for finding out whether a real conversation is possible. It is learnable through structured exposure.
gear: Places with strangers: queues, trains, events
steps: Learn the openers: the shared situation, a sincere compliment, or a genuine question about the context you are both in.
Learn to give free information — an extra detail in your answers that gives the other person something to grab.
Learn to escalate gently from facts to opinions to experiences. That progression is what turns small talk into conversation.
Practise the exit: “I am going to grab a drink, it was good to meet you” is polite and clean.
Set a weekly quota — three conversations with strangers — and treat awkward ones as reps rather than failures.
Prepare two or three current topics so you are never scrabbling.
tips: One-word answers starve a conversation. Always add a detail.
Questions people have answered a thousand times get bored answers. Ask a slightly unusual version instead.
proof: You start and sustain a ten-minute conversation with a stranger, comfortably, and part on good terms.
